assign.now: steps 2-5 landed — LayoutTool/taste (11 ideal ranges, refit on measurement), a grammar-based generator (shapes/roles/INNER), the chaos dial, and token tones. Building the search.

log.msg: TRAP: a tab driven through MCP eval is document.visibilityState=hidden, and a hidden tab runs no rendering steps — rAF never fires and ResizeObserver never delivers. The layout-space ruler kept all five shots at max-content 4184px and every one scored B 84. Cost ~30 min chasing a layout bug that was a measurement bug. Recorded in ruler.js and in the claim-tab skill; use mcp shot or headless Playwright for geometry.

Calibration run (26 good pages + 10 library/bad traps, 1280 and 3440) refit six of the eleven bands. repetition was written at 0.30-0.75 from intuition and the site measures 0.23 (p10-p90 0.09-0.42); measure narrowed to the sites own IQR 52-68; pad-share is the tightest quantity measured (median 0.037, IQR 0.033-0.047, width-independent) and gained weight; frame-gap is BIMODAL (chrome ~0.4-0.8, cards ~1.6-1.9, median in the empty middle) and lost weight; lanes is partly a page-chrome artefact (the bad/ traps score higher than the good pages); depth is root-relative AND bimodal so it weights last. A weight is evidence, not opinion.

Pointed the new rulebook at the nine hand-written presets. Ranked by worst width: landing 73, dashboard 67, masonry 62, document 61, docs 61, gallery 50, mail 49, shell 47, split 46. mail is B87 at 1280 and F49 at 390 — the sharpest argument on the site for scoring the WORST width rather than the mean. Three site-wide complaints fell out: --measure:52em is ~117 chars a line at 3440 (zero credit on five of nine), em padding does not scale (pad-share ~0 at 3440 on every preset), and repetition reads 0.95 on everything because web.js is made entirely of repeated components (real pages measure 0.23).

Three corrections to the rating tier found by running it on the presets: width-used had a CEILING that charged a full-bleed shell for spanning 99% — double-counting pad-shares complaint, now no upper penalty; width-used measured over text blocks only, so a gallery of sixteen image tiles reported spending 11% of 3440 while filling it — now over content leaves; and frame-gap/pad-share counted painted boxes with no text, so a wall of .wash swatches took frame-gap to 0.00 — now only boxes that hold text, the guard rules.js already has.

Hunt run 1: 8 sweeps x 120 seeds x 3 widths. CHAOS HURTS MONOTONICALLY — mean worst at depth 2 is 60.5 at chaos 0, 59.0 at 0.25, 56.2 at 0.5, 51.0 at 1.0. That is the number the grammar was for: the model beats the flat pick it replaced by 16%. But the single best layout in the grid (worst 81) came from chaos 0.25, not chaos 0 — chaos widens the tail both ways, which is the argument for the dial rather than for loosening the model. Depth is nearly flat (1-4 span 2.4pts, best at 2). fit is a genuine null result (screen 1.001 vs page 0.998, n=296/184).

Threw out run 1s shape table: the three rater fixes landed AFTER the sweeps started, and two of them hit exactly the ranges run 1 named as discriminating. gallery and deck are the two text-poorest shapes and were the bottom two, while width-used was still measured over text blocks only. A search is only as good as the scorer it searches against, and the first thing a search finds is the scorers bugs. Re-running five sweeps against the corrected ranges before touching any weight in model.js.

assign.now: hunt run 1 landed (chaos hurts 16%); re-running against the corrected ranges before retuning model.js. Docs and per-file notes in flight.

log.msg: Fourth rater correction, found by the taste page rating itself: scale counted DISTINCT gap values and this tiers own doc page measured 25, scoring zero. Any real page has a long tail of one-off gaps (a table border, a caption, an icon beside a word) on top of the three or four sizes it is genuinely built from. It counts the VOCABULARY now — the smallest set of values covering four fifths of the pages gaps. Presets now read scale 2-4 and the Hunt page rates itself B 80 where the taste page rated F 59.

Hunt run 2, against the corrected ranges. Seed 85 scored worst 63 under the old ranges and worst 87 under the new — same generator, same seed, a 24-point swing that was entirely the scorer. Chaos still hurts but by two thirds as much (-9.3% not -16%). The shape order RESHUFFLED: shell mid-table to first (lift 1.14), mail first to a four-way tie for third, gallery and deck recovered 8-10 points but are still the bottom two. Run 1s recommendation (raise mail) did not survive. model.js SHAPES now carries the run-2 numbers, each old weight scaled by lift cubed. Ceiling rose 81 to 87.

The honest cost of the width-used fix: it went from run 1s third-best discriminator (gap 0.26) to exactly 0.00 — this generator now clears 70% width-use so reliably the range cannot separate a good roll from a bad one. Keeping its weight anyway, because the nine hand-written presets fail it hard at 3440: a range can be saturated for one population and the sharpest thing you own for another. Five ranges (slivers, depth, repetition, scale, gap-share) carry no information for the generator at all — a result rather than a gap, since the model keeps every roll clear of the zones they exist to catch.

Two ranges were in direct CONFLICT and it took the presets to show it: pad-share as a raw share of width wants 3.7% of a 3440 band, which is 127px, which is 7em, which frame-gap calls badly over-padded. Both bands came from the same 36 pages and both are right — about different boxes. polish.js already writes the resolution (min(3.5%, 3.5em), proportional until a box gets wide then flat), so pad-share now measures against that expectation: a 300px card with 11px and a 3440 band with 56px both read 1.0. frame-gaps ceiling also had to clear 3.5, because that is where the sites own formula lands a band at 3440 — a ceiling of 3.2 made the house pattern unrepresentable.

Biggest single generator win of the session: --pad INHERITS, so the band inset the generator put on a wide top-level track was also the inset on the 300px card inside it — three ems on a card the rulebook expects ten pixels on. Every leaf now reclaims a cards pad. Measured on 14 seeds at chaos 0: mean worst 56 to 66, median 54 to 68, best 65 to 75.

A dial whose sign flips under measurement is measuring the wrong thing. Making chaos draw depth uniformly over 0..max produced FLATTER layouts at max 2 — and this rulebook rewards simplicity, so chaos measured as an improvement (mean 61 to 70 over 8 seeds). Reverted: DEPTHS now spans 0-10 instead of stopping at 5 (its keys are the vocabulary draw.js blends toward uniform, so the dials right half was unreachable at any chaos) and level() is a plain weighted pick again. Final verification sweep dispatched at n=120 to settle the sign.

Run 3, n=120, after the four fixes. Chaos sign SETTLED: mean worst 73.8 / 72.6 / 65.9 at chaos 0 / 0.25 / 1.0, monotonic, -10.7%. The padding fix was worth +8.3 points of mean fitness on the same scorer (65.5 to 73.8) — the cleanest before/after in the exercise. New ceiling 86, and it is 86 at 390, 86 at 1280 AND 86 at 3440: every earlier ceiling had one width dragging it down, and a flat curve is what the prime objective actually asks for. The shape table went flat (lift 0.98-1.12, leader n=6, under the believability floor) so SHAPES was LEFT ALONE — fitting a table that flat is fitting noise, and a loop has to be able to decline to run.

THE LESSON OF THE SESSION: a broken range discriminates beautifully. width-used, lanes and frame-gap each looked like a strong discriminator and each collapsed to a ~0.0 top-vs-bottom gap the moment its own defect was fixed. Three times is not a coincidence — a defective range separates layouts BY THE DEFECT. width-used was sorting them by how much text they happened to contain; frame-gap by how many undecorated swatches they drew. Both signals were real and reproducible; neither was about the layout. A ranges apparent power is not evidence that it is right, and a suspiciously clean ranking is the first thing to distrust.

assign.outcome: **The layout generator now searches instead of sampling, and it got measurably stronger doing it.** New: [/framework/ext/LayoutTool/taste/](/framework/ext/LayoutTool/taste/) — a third tier that rates what is GOOD (eleven weighted ideal ranges) where analyze() only says what is broken; [/framework/styles/layouts/space/hunt/](/framework/styles/layouts/space/hunt/) — the search, and where the model gets better; [/framework/dev/Claim/](/framework/dev/Claim/) — the viewport ring an agent draws around a tab it is driving, with a claim-tab MCP skill. Rebuilt: the generator draws from a grammar (shapes, roles, what-is-best-inside-what) instead of a flat pick, with a chaos dial that is a measured distance from that model and tones taken from the sites own colour tokens. Unified: gen(seed, opts) takes an options object where it took a depth, so every ext/Panel reroll button inherits the same model and chaos — with zero edits to ext/Panel. MEASURED, n=120 x 3 widths: chaos hurts monotonically (-10.7%), the padding-cascade fix was worth +8.3 points of mean fitness, and the best layout found scores 86 at 390, 86 at 1280 and 86 at 3440 — every earlier ceiling had one width dragging it down. The rulebooks own bands were refit twice, six on calibration against 36 site pages and four more on use. The lesson worth keeping: a BROKEN range discriminates beautifully, because it is measuring its own defect — three of eleven went quiet the moment their bug was fixed.
